data.gender_notes: Hebe is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Hebe was the goddess of youth and the personification of the eternal youth of the gods. She was the cupbearer of the gods, ensuring their eternal youth and vitality by constantly refilling their cups with nectar and ambrosia. The name Hebe carries the meaning “Goddess of youth and prosperity” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hebe usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of youth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes renewal, vitality, and the continuity of life.
data.etymology: Hebe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of youth and prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hebe total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Hebe's role as the cupbearer of the gods in Greek mythology showcases the importance of hospitality and the sharing of food and drink in ancient Greek culture. Her presence at the table of the gods symbolizes the communal and celebratory nature of their feasts, emphasizing the power and influence of the gods and their connection to their followers.
data.spiritual_significance: Hebe represents the concept of eternal youth, vitality, and the continuity of life. In a spiritual context, her name can be seen as a reminder of the importance of maintaining one's physical, emotional, and spiritual health and vitality throughout the different stages of life. By invoking Hebe's name, one may ask for her blessings of longevity, vitality, and the ability to keep the spirit of youthfulness alive. Additionally, her role as a cupbearer can be seen as a symbol of the Christian concept of the Eucharist, as both Hebe and the Eucharist serve to bring the divine presence closer to the people.
